ff99SB.cite: Hornak 2006 (ff99SB); HYP residue as distributed in GROMACS amber99sb.ff
ff99SB.derived_note: HYP template re-encoded from GROMACS amber99sb.ff/aminoacids.rtp into OpenMM XML (OpenMM's amber99sb.xml has no HYP). Types/charges copied verbatim; bonded terms come from the ff99SB class tables. Equivalence to GROMACS ffbonded.itp is unit-tested.

ff14SB.cite: Maier 2015; OpenMM conversion of AmberTools 17.6 leaprc.protein.ff14SB

ff19SB.cite: Tian 2020; OpenMM conversion of AmberTools 24.8 leaprc.protein.ff19SB

C36m.cite: Huang 2017; toppar_c36_jul24 conversions: OpenMM 8.6.1 charmm36_2024.xml (par_all36m_prot.prm) + HYP residue from openmmforcefields charmm36_d_modified.xml (toppar_all36_prot_modify_res.str)
C36m.derived_note: HYP <Residue> element copied verbatim out of charmm36_d_modified.xml into its own file. Loading the whole modified-residue file is not possible for peptides: it also defines graph-identical DPRO, HZP (hydroxyproline with CGenFF atom types) and an AMGY patch, which OpenMM cannot distinguish from PRO, HYP and ACE. No parameter values are changed; AllowPatch references to patches defined only in that file (AMGY, DMCT) are dropped.

C36mGP.cite: Pantelopulos & Best 2025 definition applied to the C36m files above
C36mGP.derived_note: RECONSTRUCTION: CMAP grids whose central C-alpha class is CT2 (Gly) or CP1 (Pro/Hyp) multiplied by 0.5, per the published definition. The authors' own files (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.15354101) could not be downloaded here and were NOT compared.

_structures.source: PDB 1CAG (two GitHub mirrors, coordinate records identical)
_structures.ace_hyp_nme: chain A Hyp20 + caps from Pro19/Gly21 backbone atoms
_structures.pog3_triple_helix: chains A 19-27, B 49-57, C 79-87 (same sequence register) + caps
